executive_summary: Marico’s September quarter is a better quality growth print because India volume and international constant-currency growth are both strong. Softer copra and portfolio mix support earnings, but A&P reinvestment, Saffola’s reset and a premium multiple mean the margin rebound should not simply be extrapolated.
research_stance: Strong volume and mix execution; distinguish commodity-led margin recovery from a durable earnings rebase.
results_analysis: The local consolidated September 2026 quarter records revenue ₹3,897.00 crore, operating profit ₹709.00 crore and PAT ₹558.00 crore. Revenue changed +13.0% YoY and -1.5% QoQ; PAT changed +29.2% YoY and -14.4% QoQ.

Operating profit changed +26.6% YoY and -13.4% QoQ. The calculated operating-profit/sales margin is 18.19%, versus 16.23% a year earlier and 20.70% in June. These calculations use a consistently rounded local series; management EBITDA may use a different scope or definition.

Local consolidated PAT is ₹558 crore; management describes 31% PAT growth while the consistently rounded local series gives 29.2%. The exact attribution or recurrence bridge has not been established, so the difference remains unresolved rather than being explained speculatively. FY26 CFO ₹2,084 crore and free cash flow ₹1,772 crore support the cash-generating franchise, but these historic cash flows do not fix a fair entry multiple.

Price and financial dates differ: the cleaned close used here is ₹902.00 on 2026-11-12; the public-financial snapshot is dated 2026-11-07. The screenshot price is not treated as a live or verified valuation input. Local public-financial-data parquets, September 2026 quarter; amounts rounded to ₹ crore.

valuation.assessment: The available price/EPS calculation is about 58×. The cash-generating franchise and 10% India volume growth are supportive, but a commodity-assisted FY27 profit upgrade does not guarantee a higher permanent growth rate. Valuation should reflect normalized copra costs, recurringA&P needs and brand profitability rather than capitalising peak gross-margin relief.
assumptions: At the 12 November adjusted close of ₹902.00, the available four-quarter EPS sum is ₹15.53, implying approximately 58.1× earnings and a 1.72% earnings yield. This is a price/available-EPS calculation, not a forecast or a fully normalized multiple.

A 20% contraction in the earnings multiple would require 25% cumulative EPS growth merely to keep the share price unchanged; dividends are excluded. This is algebraic sensitivity, not a prediction of the exit multiple.
No point fair value is assigned from an unverified terminal multiple or FY29 aspiration; brand-level recognized revenue and cash contribution are needed.

business_economics: India 10% volume growth and international 13% CCgrowth are stronger evidence than reported revenue alone, particularly during copra deflation. Parachute’s 13% volume growth with price reductions suggests demand and share momentum, but reported share is management-attributed and channel health still needs verification.

The portfolio is moving toward foods, premium personal care and digital brands. Their faster growth can diversify the franchise, butARR, recognized sales, segment contribution and customer-acquisition costs differ. A larger share of new businesses does not automatically mean a higher consolidated return on capital.
earnings_quality: The gross-margin recovery reflects softer copra, portfolio mix and operational improvement, while 44% higherA&P reinvests part of the benefit. Copra being 35% below a past peak is not the same as a 35% year-on-year decline in consumed raw-material costs, so a direct margin arithmetic from spot prices is inappropriate.

Management’s 31% PAT-growth statement and the local 29.2% calculation remain different. The prior report speculated about attribution/recurrence, but that explanation was not established. Current local PAT ₹558 cr remains the numeric anchor, and the exact comparable profit bridge is an open question.
capital_allocation: FY26CFO ₹2,084 cr and FCF ₹1,772 cr support the cash-generation record. The capital-allocation question is whether funding acquired growth brands, distribution andA&P continues to produce incremental cash earnings rather than simply sustaining faster reported revenue.

Saffola’s deliberate pruning of low-margin variants is an economically sensible experiment if it improves contribution and cash returns after the 2–3quarterreset. It should be judged against retained customers, premium-product mix and profitability, not excused indefinitely as rationalisation.
valuation_logic: At about 58× available EPS, cash quality alone does not establish an attractive entry price. A20% multiple contraction requires 25% EPS growth merely to keep price unchanged. The FY27 mid-20s EBITDA upgrade helps, but management explicitly retains a mid-teens growth view for subsequent years.

The FY29₹20,000 cr aspiration has no full bottom-upbuild disclosed on the call. A valuation should therefore model named drivers—India volume, price/cost cycles,CCinternational growth and recognized new-brand contribution—rather than solve backward to that headline.
peer_positioning: Large consumer-staples peers help compare pricing power, distribution, cash conversion andA&Pintensity. Yet Marico’s concentrated coconut-oil exposure and growing digital/food portfolio make an unadjusted category-average multiple a weak valuation argument.

Compare normalized margins through both inflation and deflation, and assess whether new brands add cash contribution after promotion and acquisition amortisation. Standalone digital-brandARR multiples are especially poor substitutes for listed-parent cash flow.
